en: The Guru, for whom the illusory net of duality has dissolved through the most mature of his own direct experiences,
[reveals] that which is hidden from those of wicked intellect burdened by a flood of sins, yet is manifest to those endowed with wisdom;
though it has been perfectly experienced within his own heart, he [speaks] this for the sake of awakening his excellent disciples.
He truly recollected his own [nature] as the source of all worlds through his own vision. || 1 ||

This entire duality has arisen within me as something false, imagined by the mind; it is like water produced merely through delusion in the wind-swept sky where no water exists. If this is indeed so, then this entire visible world is neither "I" nor is it mine.
I am pure, I am indivisible, my body being composed solely of the consciousness of mature bliss. || 2 ||
This body is not my self, for it is insentient and determined to be like a wall;
nor am I the vital breath, which is like air held within a bellows.
Nor am I that mind, which is as fickle as a monkey and corrupted by miserliness.
The intellect in one who acts like a Buddha is merely hypocrisy; it is not the blinding darkness of ignorance. || 3 ||
I am clearly not even the khadira wood, for I am eternally distinct from those things due to my similarity to the water shining in the sky; I am the all-seeing one, like the solar light.
Free from contact with visible objects, I am of a perfectly full nature, like the ether.
However, in accordance with the actual state of things, I am like the ocean [of which] waves and so forth are [the parts]. || 4 ||
I am non-dual; I am the stainless sky of consciousness; I am full; I am bodiless; I am without senses; I am utterly devoid of the category of vital breaths;
I am one whose mind is liberated from impurity; I am the treasury of dissolving discernment.
I am free from illusion, I am without interval, and I am the vast and mature light. || 5 ||
Indeed, there is nothing other than Me; if anything appears as an object of consciousness, that is false, like fire in a *guñjā* berry.
I am the substratum for all conceptualization; I am the witness of everything, equal in essence, peaceful, and sinless.
I am full, I am free from duality, I am the vast space, and I am eternal.
Regarding me, who am this ultimate reality to be known through the Upanishads, what contradiction can there be in my self-luminosity?
For everything shines precisely because of my presence; just as a person perceiving everything made manifest by the power of sunlight does not perceive that very sun itself.
Therefore, I am that certain, indubitable, and absolute light which is Śiva alone.
I am of the nature of eternal manifestation; I am the pure, eternal sky; I am peaceful;
I am composed of eternal bliss; I am one from whom the great darkness of delusion has departed. The entire reality of the supreme truth, which is my own and free from all impurity, has been realized.
I am that which is to be attained by the liberated, known as Kaivalya (absolute liberation), in which all notions of duality have been cast aside.

Just like the duality experienced in a dream, the duality of the waking state as well is merely mental and false; thus, having abandoned it, I am of the singular nature of the pure, conscious, and stainless heart.
Or rather, this entire world of objects of knowledge is incessantly my very own form.
Having known this and abandoned it, I am mature and profound like the great ocean that has cast away its breath. || 9 ||

What is there to be gone to here for me, who am entirely complete and of unbroken form? What duty remains here for me, whose body is actionless and whose sole nature is liberation? For me, who am non-dual, there is nothing else to be abandoned, nor is there any other goal to be attained.
Today I am at peace, pure like a cloud freed from water and stainless.
What was not obtained before this, and what is now gained through investigation and the like,
such that I am perpetually ablaze as the very nature of that bliss?
Or rather, what need is there here even for me to expect further false investigation and so forth?
In that state which is free from duality and non-duality and characterized by equanimity, supreme silence is held to be the highest approval.

What is there for me, who am fully enlightened and directly perceiving, to hear? And what is there for me to reflect upon, since I possess the light of certainty? For me, whose very form is the dissolution of the distinction between the meditator and the object of meditation, there is indeed nothing at all to be meditated upon.
Or rather, my constant meditative absorption is in the single great essence which is the self of all.

Even the discrimination between self and non-self does not please me as formulated by the learned, since there is no "non-self" apart from that which exists as an object of experience; who indeed is capable of making such a distinction?
Alas, those who have not perceived the Self engage in the contemplation of false doctrines and fallacious reasoning!
Only those who are deluded do not reach the further shore; those of firm intellect remain silent, like a mountain of stone. || 13 ||

In accordance with the true state of reality, alas, I am no particular entity whatsoever; nor do I appear as such to the continuous vision that transcends the reach of speech and mind. I am sinless, I am fearless, and I am free from the stain of evil doubt.
I am the mature radiance of a light that is perfectly tranquil, incomparable, and cool.
I, who was previously pure and free from all mental constructs, am awakened; for from me this world arose, by me it is sustained,
and into me alone it goes to dissolution— salutations ever to that which is without any substrate.
Salutations to me, whose self consists of truth, bliss, and consciousness, and who possesses vast wisdom. || 15 ||
There exists that which is the nature of existence, consciousness, and bliss, eternal; neither "I" nor "you" exists, and this entire perceived world is false—it does not exist at all.
Know this clearly, O friend: that which has been spoken by me to you out of compassion is the truth.
Have faith, O sinless one; if your intellect is pure, let your doubt cease.
This mature realization,

which shines forth of its own accord having been attained by the head of the beautiful Lord of the Gods, should be granted only to one whose mind is charmingly and easily awakened by its natural elegance; it must not be given to one whose intellect is milked of wisdom by delusion or whose inner heart is corrupt.
If that ketaki flower has fallen into the reach of a monkey's hand, does it still shine? || 17 ||
Thus, in the work of the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavat-pūjyapāda, the illustrious wandering mendicant teacher (paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya).
The mature experience is complete.
